lead.headline: SpaceX catches a Starship returning from orbit for the first time
lead.dek: Tower arms grabbed Ship 42 at Starbase on Saturday, 22 hours after liftoff; Friday's booster was lost over the Gulf
body: SpaceX's launch tower caught a Starship upper stage descending from orbit at Starbase, Texas, at 4:20 p.m. ET Saturday, the first recovery of the vehicle's ship from space. The catch came about 22 hours and 14 orbits after Friday's 5:47 p.m. liftoff, the company said.

Ship 42 reached an orbit about 165 miles up, released 26 Starlink V3 satellites and came down belly-first through low cloud before relighting three of its six Raptor engines, flipping vertical and settling into the tower's arms, CBS News reported. SpaceX said the heat shield appeared healthy. The company had caught three boosters before Saturday but never a ship.

The Super Heavy booster was not recovered: SpaceX said an automated abort during coast sent it to a Gulf splashdown after its boostback burn ended early on low fuel, and it broke apart, Euronews reported. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman called the catch "almost magic"; NASA is counting on a Starship variant for the Artemis Moon landing it targets for 2028.

briefs.headline: Airlines cancel 5,000 more flights Saturday as the FAA recovers
briefs.summary: FlightAware counted more than 5,000 cancellations Saturday after Friday's ground stop; Secretary Sean Duffy said a contractor's router swap at a remote FAA site flooded the network, and the FAA expects full recovery by the end of Sunday.

briefs.headline: CMS gives states until July to enforce Medicaid work rules
briefs.summary: The agency told states Friday they may wait until July 1 to drop expansion enrollees who miss the 80-hour-a-month requirement that takes effect Jan. 1; Nebraska, first to start, denied 533 people, mostly over paperwork.

briefs.headline: Peltola tops 50% in Alaska's Senate count as ballots keep coming
briefs.summary: Mary Peltola had 50.1% to Sen. Dan Sullivan's 46.1% after Saturday's count of more than 283,000 ballots, enough to win without ranked-choice tabulation if it holds; counting continues through Wednesday.

briefs.headline: US loses measles elimination status, Wall Street Journal reports
briefs.summary: The Pan American Health Organization revoked the status after a year of continuous spread, Al Jazeera reported citing the Journal; states count 10 deaths and more than 5,400 cases this year, against the CDC's six deaths.

briefs.headline: Zelensky says US raised NATO entry for a Donbas pullout
briefs.summary: He told journalists Friday that U.S. negotiators asked after the Abu Dhabi round whether Ukraine would leave the Donbas it still holds in exchange for membership; nothing was agreed and Ukrainians would decide, he said.

briefs.headline: Iran claims a second drone attack on a US base in Bahrain
briefs.summary: The Revolutionary Guards said six drones targeted a U.S. radar at the Riffa helicopter base early Sunday; Bahrain's military said its air defenses intercepted the attacks after sirens and two shelter alerts, France24 reported.

briefs.headline: ASEAN summit opens in Manila under energy and sea strains
briefs.summary: Leaders of more than 20 countries opened the 49th summit Sunday with the Hormuz energy crisis and South China Sea disputes on the agenda; China sent Premier Li Qiang, Russia sent Sergey Lavrov, and Trump is due Nov. 17.

briefs.headline: Guatemala declares a 30-day state of siege in Zacapa and Izabal
briefs.summary: The government decreed the measure after armed attacks killed seven on Nov. 13; it limits movement, assembly and gun ownership and allows searches without a court order, and the army said it deployed 400 to 600 soldiers.

briefs.headline: Kessel Fire grows to 368 acres, 90% contained after back-burns
briefs.summary: Division of Forestry Director Jeremy Jones said Saturday night the Cacapon Mountain fire grew with planned burnouts; a separate Largent fire was put out Friday, trails stay closed and a virtual community meeting is set for 2 p.m. Sunday.

briefs.headline: DHS says 40,000 on expanded Medicaid may miss new work rules
briefs.summary: The department said about 40,000 of some 160,000 expansion enrollees have not been identified as meeting the 80-hour requirement or an exemption before Jan. 1, up from a 33,000 estimate, West Virginia Watch reported Saturday.

briefs.headline: Marshall reads 75 names at its 56th Fountain Ceremony
briefs.summary: Keynote speaker Jeff Heath, who lost his parents and godparents in the 1970 plane crash, said Saturday that Huntington "came to our aid"; a white rose was laid for each of the 75 victims.

briefs.headline: Lawmakers press DHS over a stalled child care law
briefs.summary: At Monday's interim health committee the department said it is more than three months behind the law's deadlines and may struggle to fund it within $129 million; Del. Mike Pushkin cited delayed provider payments, WCHS reported Friday.

regional.item: MHN and the Huntington City Mission opened a $2.7M, 10-bed medical respite facility on the Mission campus Friday.
CAMC's $45M Teays Valley expansion is now due in December 2027, a year later than planned, The Herald-Dispatch reported Sunday.
Parkersburg's 160-year-old Logan Memorial United Methodist Church, organized in 1866 for Black residents, has closed after membership fell to about 20.
Summersville Lake State Park is one of four parks now taking 2027 reservations for 32 new glamping tents, the governor's office said Friday.

away.item: A North Bennington man, 67, died Tuesday when the car he was riding in hit a propane truck on Route 313 in Arlington.

hotspots.item: No. 13 Webster County's football season ended Saturday with a 50-36 loss at No. 4 East Hardy in the Class A playoffs' first round.
Surf City won a $208,914 state coastal-access grant Friday for an elevated boardwalk, kayak launch and parking on Deep Creek at Goldsboro Avenue.

briefs.headline: Prince George park gets an eight-metre bridge built for frogs
briefs.summary: The crossing over an amphibian migration route at Shane Lake in Forests for the World was finished Nov. 12 by the city, Nahanni Construction and partners, CBC reported, after a forester flagged thousands of crushed young amphibians in 2022.

briefs.headline: Judge dismisses a defamation suit against a Quesnel councillor
briefs.summary: Justice Tindale ruled Coun. Laurey-Anne Roodenburg's 2024 council remarks about a residential school book Pat Morton handed out were not defamatory and awarded costs; Morton said she will appeal, My Cariboo Now reported Friday.

briefs.headline: Second storm brings wind and up to 150 mm of rain to the South Coast
briefs.summary: Environment Canada forecast 40 to 70 mm from Squamish to Whistler and up to 150 mm on western Vancouver Island by Sunday, with wind warnings on the Island; Pemberton stays on evacuation alert and Highway 99 has reopened east of the village.

briefs.headline: Zeballos marks a week without power as weather turns back crews
briefs.summary: BC Hydro tried to fly a crew into the mountains Saturday and was turned back, CHEK News reported; the village's 203 customers have been dark since Nov. 7 and a landslide keeps homes under evacuation order.

briefs.headline: Fifth soldier dies of injuries from the CFB Wainwright training fire
briefs.summary: Pte. William Douglas Dal Bianco of 3 PPCLI died Friday in an Ontario hospital from the Oct. 17 grass fire that swept a live-fire exercise, the Defence Department said; 24 soldiers remain in hospital.

briefs.headline: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth on Wednesday
briefs.summary: The probe will be the first human-made object a full light-day out, more than 16 billion miles, on Nov. 18, NASA said; its signals take 24 hours to arrive, and the agency asks the public to flash "VGR" in Morse code Tuesday evening.

briefs.headline: Independent analysis recovers the M87 black hole's ring
briefs.summary: CSIRO researchers re-ran Event Horizon Telescope data with a machine-learning method trained on photos of cats, dogs and cars and got the same ring diameter and orientation, they report in Nature; finer details differ.

briefs.headline: North China rocks point to subduction 3.95 billion years ago
briefs.summary: Zircon isotopes from the Shimen Complex in Hebei show surface-touched material was buried more than 50 km deep, Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences researchers report in Nature, implying an early plate-tectonic-like event.

briefs.headline: One CRISPR infusion cut monkeys' blood fats for three years
briefs.summary: A single base-editing dose against ANGPTL3 cut the protein about 94% and triglycerides about 43% in 10 monkeys followed for three years, Verve Therapeutics, the Eli Lilly unit that funded and led the work, reports in Nature.

briefs.headline: Australia's central bank sees AI strain on young workers
briefs.summary: A Reserve Bank of Australia study found little labour-market disruption overall, but in the most AI-exposed jobs workers aged 15 to 24 show weaker employment and higher unemployment than older workers; the author calls it descriptive.

briefs.headline: Models trained on eight children's home speech learn words
briefs.summary: Princeton researchers trained a model on each child's recorded speech, with no text; with nightly replay of recent input the models segmented phonemes and picked out thousands of word forms, they report in Science. None learned meanings.

briefs.headline: KAIST lip-reading model fills in its surest words first
briefs.summary: A diffusion language model that decodes confident words first and uses them as context reached a 19.4% word error rate on the LRS3 lip-reading set, the lowest using only that data, KAIST said in a preprint not yet peer reviewed.

weather_ear: Sunday's forecast follows from Jim Claudtore at 7:15.
kicker: Summers-New River carries no regional line today; Cape Verde votes in a presidential race that includes its first woman candidate.

art.caption: SpaceX's Starship upper stage, engines lit, hangs above the catch arms of its launch tower at Starbase, Texas, before Saturday's catch.
